tagline: A Mount Pleasant road beside two community histories.
intro: From Whipple Road to 7th Street, Mathis Ferry Road runs through Mount Pleasant. Its scenic designation came with protection for larger trees in the highway right-of-way. Houses have filled in along the route since 1988, and the state still counts it as having kept most of its scenic qualities.

Nearby excursions tell different stories of community. I’On was planned around traditional neighborhood design; at Remley Point Cemetery in Scanlonville, residents fought a proposal to move graves for a private homestead, and a judge ruled against development of the cemetery.

moments.title: I’On
moments.text: A planned neighborhood in Mount Pleasant built around a village square, with sites for churches and schools, after a lengthy legal contest over its development.

moments.title: Remley Point Cemetery
moments.text: In Scanlonville, marked graves preserve an African American community’s burial ground that residents went to court to protect.
